issues: The binary search approach evaluates an O(N) area function 100 times, resulting in a time complexity of O(100 * N), which does redundant recalculations over non-intersecting squares and is relatively inefficient. An O(N log N) sweep-line algorithm is much faster and computes the exact intersection analytically, circumventing any potential floating-point precision constraints inherent to iterative approximation.
